paths_note: Evidence paths are given in the current layout. Auditor scratch files (Lean experiments, disassembly, scripts and their output) are not kept; audits/check_code.py replaces the code checks.
scope: Independent read-only audit of the ONDO proof (token-kit/tokens/ondo, Lean 4 v4.35.0 on EthLib 62dbd687 and usdt-verify d0e684c5, both pins confirmed by git rev-parse in upstream/ and in lake-manifest.json). No Lean was built (no Lean on this Mac); nothing outside audits/ondo/ was written. Evidence: the hand-written Lean files read in full (Seq, Sep, SigSupply, Sig, Readable, Code, Map, Dispatch, Arith header, Test/Axioms), Gen/ files read by statement only (with show.py / cases.py, which drop readSlot wrappers and print each disjunct of a *_ends definition), the bytes in survey/tokens/ONDO, the verified Solidity source (fetched read-only from Sourcify into src/Ondo.sol: solc 0.8.3, runs 100, same compiler as SOURCE.md), three public eth_call reads of the live contract, and the logs logs/ondo.* and logs/ondo.*. Date 2026-11-12.
checked_ok: Code: CODE_NAT in Ondo/Code/Bytes.lean is the same hex string as survey/tokens/ONDO/runtime.hex and data/ondo.runtime.hex (first byte 0x60, so no leading zero byte is lost in the Nat form); CODE_SIZE 11822 = byte count. keccak256 with my own Python keccak = 7643c7b2...037e = EXPECTED_HASH in Test/Hash.lean = SOURCE.md.

Selector table: the 42 'DUP1 PUSH4 k EQ PUSH2 d JUMPI' entries in the bytes equal ENTRIES in Ondo/Map.lean (same order, same destinations, every destination a JUMPDEST). The 42 keys equal keccak of the 42 ABI function signatures of abi.json; none missing, none extra. delta_step (Invariant.lean:1813) matches on all 42 indices of ENTRIES (index 7 = delegateBySig is excluded by hsel7 and handled in SigSupply.lean); config functions 40 + readonly_loops 1 + prefix_functions 1 = 42.

Outside calls in the bytes (metadata tail excluded): exactly one STATICCALL (pc 5176, after GAS at 5175 = config 'stops'); no CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, CREATE, CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT. Opcode counts SSTORE 17, SLOAD 67, SHA3 78, TIMESTAMP 6, NUMBER 2, CHAINID 1 match status.json. So there is no reentrancy surface; the only callee is the precompile at address 1.

Role constants in Readable.lean (MINTER_ROLE, TRANSFER_ROLE, TIMELOCK_UPDATE_ROLE) equal keccak of the role names. EIP-712 constants in Sig.lean (domainSepName, delegStruct, delegDigest) equal keccak of the source strings and the 0x1901 prefix: the digest IS the EIP-712 digest of the source, only not restated in words.

Soundness hygiene: text scan of tokens/ondo/OndoVerify and TokenKit: no sorry (one hit is the word sorryAx in a comment), admit, axiom declaration, native_decide, bv_decide, unsafe, implemented_by, opaque, extern, skipKernelTC. lakefile has no extra Lean options. Test/Axioms.lean prints axioms of supply_preserved_real, inv_calls, process_step_inv, calls_process and every readable theorem (2115 #print axioms lines), and its last command scans every constant of every imported OndoVerify and TokenKit module, failing on any declared axiom or any non-standard axiom; no skip list beyond 4 generated names that no file declares (supply_valueSent, supply_short, supply_other, supply_delegateBySigTail).

Counts: 4556 theorem declarations in OndoVerify (rg), B* 2266, P* 1731 with 341 ok_ theorems, Loops 158, Arith 25, Sep 21, Frame 147, Invariant 84, SigSupply 7, Sig 2, Seq 10, Readable 18, Sanity 78, segment files/theorems Tt 3/33, Vest 3/93, Core 11/77, MvSrc 13/129, MvDst 38/304, Wck 79/829: all equal status.json theorem_counts. logs/ondo.axioms: 'theorems checked: 2115', 'count matches Test/Axioms.lean: 2115', 'AXIOM SCAN OK: 99612 constants (99174 theorems)', AXRC=0; ondo.log ends 'Build completed successfully (1728 jobs).' EXIT=0; the 2026-11-11 log logs/ondo.* says the same.

Dead-branch table (config/dead.json, 50 rules): gen_paths.py only drops a branch after emitting a Lean proof that it is decided ('have hd<n> : ... := by dead_omega ...'; 1162 such proofs in 150 Gen files). A wrong rule fails the build, so the table cannot drop a live path. The only WEAKENS switch in use is 'stops' [5175] for delegateBySig, and that function is closed by hand in Sig.lean / SigSupply.lean under the real runner.

No hypothesis false for EthLib's real runner was found. supply_preserved / delta_step take EndsL for ANY runner; delta_step_real / supply_preserved_real fix processRunner and use the real Precompiles.Ecrecover.compute through recoveredWord (ok_delegateBySig_real, Sig.lean:137), nothing assumed about its output. No hypothesis restates its conclusion (mint_amounts' hne is one keccak fact implied by Sep.total; delegate_readable's two membership premises only fix the free list D).

Completeness theorems: the 42 ok_<fn> theorems take only hfork, hsize', hsel, start, hrun, hok; the 290 segment theorems add memory-shape facts that the caller discharges through the <seg>_mem lemmas. Chain wiring checked: ok_transfer passes (arg1, arg0, CALLER) to tt0_ends, so the vesting check of vest0_ends is on the caller; ok_transferFrom passes (arg2, arg1, arg0), so it is on src.

Vesting paths against the verified source: vest0_ends, vest1_ends, vest2_ends (Gen/PVest0..2.lean) each have exactly 8 disjuncts, and they are the 8 cases of _transferTokens + _getFreedBalance in src/Ondo.sol: initialBalance = 0 (no check); passedAllVestingPeriods (amount <= balance); after the cliff for tranche 1 with elapsed <= 15811200 and capped, tranche 2 with elapsed <= 47433600 and capped, seed (the capped seed case is proved dead: elapsed <= 60566400 when not passedAll, dead.json rule 0); at or before the cliff (initialBalance <= balance, amount <= balance - initialBalance). The overflow check cliff + 60566400 < 2^256 and the enum check investorType <= 2 appear as conditions. No vesting path is missing.

mint_readable / mint_amounts (Readable.lean:216, 242) match the source: MINTER_ROLE, dst != 0, safe96 on amount and on totalSupply, add96 cap; only slot 4 and balances[dst] change; no checkpoint write.

Sanity witnesses: the 42 *_runs theorems of Sanity/Zero.lean are closed (hypothesis hfork only) real runs from sState C [...] with explicit role slots set (mint_runs sets MINTER_ROLE of CALLER1, grantRole_p5_runs sets DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, updateTrancheBalance_runs sets TIMELOCK_UPDATE_ROLE), so the writer paths of mint, approve, grantRole, revokeRole, renounceRole, updateCliffTimestamp, enableTransfer and updateTrancheBalance are non-vacuous.

findings.claim: status.json main_theorems 'process_step_inv / calls_process: A top-level message (processMessage) to the token keeps Inv; a finite sequence of successful calls and of steps that leave the storage of the token alone (Calls) keeps Inv (inv_calls).' README fix-round text: 'the shared library token-kit/TokenKit/Seq/ ... is applied to 13 tokens through a Tx.lean file each. LINK and WBTC have no Tx.lean.'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Exactly the UNI-1 finding of the ten-token audit, not fixed for ONDO. inv_calls only follows a chain of steps, each either a GoodCall (one frame of CODE run by processRunner, started at pc 0, with RealSep and NoDelegation1 for that message) or 'Untouched' (every storage word of C the same). Untouched is PROVED only for a top-level message that ends with an error (untouched_process_failed); for every other change of state it is ASSUMED by the constructor Calls.other. A transaction to another contract (a router, a governor, a vesting or airdrop contract) that calls ONDO inside is neither: it changes ONDO storage and its top-level code is not CODE. So 'finite sequences' covers only histories made of direct calls to ONDO plus changes assumed not to touch ONDO. ONDO has no Tx.lean: the kit theorems Seq.processMessage_good_local / processTransaction_good / chain_good (any depth, whole transactions, any list) are not used, and the Untouched assumption is not in the status.json assumptions list (only the code = CODE / no-precompile hypotheses are). The README sentence implies ONDO got the transaction lift; in fact only 11 tokens use TokenKit.Seq (bnb, dai, ena, pepe, qnt, shib, uni, usdd, usde, wbt, weth: rg for processTransaction_good / chain_good), ONDO and SKY do not.

findings.claim: status.json assumptions: 'Sep (callKeys message) (ckKeys message state) role ... This is a statement about keccak that cannot be proved in Lean and is believed true'; 'hdel / NoDelegation1 ... from Pectra, the account at address 1 holds no EIP-7702 delegation code'; 'Inv is assumed before the call'. README fix-round: 'the no keccak collision assumption is cut down to a short, named list of hash facts per token (5 to 33), shown for one concrete case'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Every supply theorem of ONDO is an implication from Sep / RealSep, NoDelegation1 (real-runner ones) and Inv at the start, and none of the three is shown to hold for even one concrete state and call: no Lean term of type Sep or RealSep exists in the project, NoDelegation1 is never discharged, and there is no base case (no Seq.ZeroBase / inv_zeroBase). The audits/ fix 5 and fix 6 that UNI, DAI, ENA, USDD, USDE and SKY got (Instance.lean: inv_start, noDelegation1_sState, realSep_m0_iff reducing RealSep to a short named KeyFacts list, a closed supply_m0) was not done for ONDO, so the README's 'named list of hash facts per token, shown for one concrete case' does not hold for ONDO. Each Sep field is a plausible keccak fact (finitely many keys, each against 2^160 balance slots; the ck field is 2^32 x 2^160 pairs per delegate, about 2^-64 collision chance per delegate for a random function), so I found no reason to think Sep is false; it is unproved and unexhibited.

findings.claim: status.json theorem_counts.sanity_witnesses '42 real runs in Sanity/Zero.lean' and vacuity 'scripts/vacuity_scan.py (z3) over the 1115 distinct generated paths: 0 vacuous ... The vacuity scan (z3) covers the paths without a witness: every one of them is satisfiable.'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The 42 runs cover 36 of the 42 functions. No Lean witness exists for any success path of transfer, transferFrom, delegate, delegateBySig, getFreedBalance, getPriorVotes, nor for 7 of 8 getVestedBalance paths, nor for any tt / vest / core / mvSrc / mvDst / wck segment. So for the three functions that move tokens or votes there is no machine-checked evidence that a successful run exists in the model; if every success path of transfer were vacuous, delta_transfer and the vote frame theorems would still compile. The z3 scan does not close this: (1) it is a Python development check, not Lean ('nothing it prints is trusted'); (2) every storage read, keccak and call-data word is a FREE variable, keyed by its printed text, so two reads of the same slot written differently (mapSlot (bitwiseAnd a2 M160) 6 versus mapSlot (bitwiseAnd M160 (bitwiseAnd M160 a2)) 6, both in vest0_ends) can take different values: 'sat' is an over-approximation, only 'unsat' is meaningful; (3) it checks each segment's paths.json entry separately (transfer, tt0, vest0, core0, mvSrc0, ... are separate keys), never the composed chain transfer -> tt -> vest -> core -> mvSrc -> mvDst -> wck. Path hypothesis sets themselves are not contradictory where they were checked: each dropped branch is Lean-proved dead.

findings.suggested_fix: Add one concrete successful transfer (sender with no lock, transferAllowed set, no delegates), one transferFrom, one delegate (from a holder with a nonzero balance, so one checkpoint is written) and one delegateBySig with a real signature (as UNI and DAI have PermitRun.lean), composed through the segment ends. Reword status.json: '42 runs over 36 functions; the z3 scan treats storage reads as free words and checks segments one by one, so it is evidence, not proof, of non-vacuity'.

findings.claim: README headline 'supply invariant for all 42 functions, votes and vesting paths included'; status not_covered: 'The vesting rule ... proved only as generated path theorems (vest<i>_ends, core<i>_ends, tt<i>_ends) ... there is no readable corollary'; brief: is the per-path vesting result consistent with the real rule, is any path missing.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Consistent and complete, but only as a disjunction. vest0_ends / vest1_ends / vest2_ends each have exactly the 8 cases of the source (see checked_ok), with the exact branch conditions, and ok_transfer / ok_transferFrom imply one of them for src (= caller for transfer). What no theorem says is the rule in words, and transfer_readable / transferFrom_readable mention only the amount bound and the transferAllowed / TRANSFER_ROLE gate, so a reader of the readable layer sees no vesting at all. Plain-word rule (what the 8 cases together say): let B = initialBalance of src (investorBalances[src] >> 8, low 96 bits), t = its type (low byte, must be 0, 1 or 2), c = cliffTimestamp, now = block timestamp, bal = balances[src] before the call. If B = 0 there is no vesting check. Else the call reverts unless c + 60566400 < 2^256, and a successful transfer of amount a satisfies a <= bal - L where L, the locked amount, is: B if now <= c (and the call also needs B <= bal); 0 if now > c + 60566400; otherwise with e = now - c: for t = 0, L = B - floor(B * min(e, 15811200) / 15811200); for t = 1, L = B - floor(B * min(e, 47433600) / 47433600); for t = 2 (seed), L = B - (floor(floor(B * e / 60566400) * 2 / 3) + floor(B / 3)). The path theorems imply this rule case by case, but no Lean theorem states it, so it is not checked that the 8 disjuncts together equal it.
findings.evidence: token-kit/tokens/ondo/OndoVerify/Ondo/Gen/PVest0.lean:1743 'def vest0_ends' (8 disjuncts by cases.py); token-kit/tokens/ondo/OndoVerify/Ondo/Gen/PTt0.lean:295 tt0_ends calls vest0_ends with 'a0 a1 a2 a3'; token-kit/tokens/ondo/OndoVerify/Ondo/Gen/PTransfer.lean ok_transfer ends 'tt0_ends fork message state substate (gas - 604) s (arg1) (arg0) CALLER ...'; token-kit/tokens/ondo/OndoVerify/Ondo/Readable.lean:318-326 transfer_readable conclusion '(loadWord message.data 36 32).toNat < 2 ^ 96 and TransferGate ...'; source Ondo.sol (audit scratch, not kept):860-893 (_transferTokens), :989-1021 (_getFreedBalance), :413-460 (_getTrancheInfo, _proportionAvailable); constants 15811200 / 47433600 / 60566400 are the immutables in config/dead.json rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Readable.transfer_vesting: under the same hypotheses as transfer_readable, 'B != 0 -> amount <= bal - lockedAt B t c now' with lockedAt defined as above, proved from tt0_ends -> vest0_ends by cases (each case is word_omega on the conditions already there); same for transferFrom on src. Then the README can say 'vesting rule proved' instead of 'vesting paths'.

findings.claim: status.json not_covered[0]: 'Stretch invariant (latest checkpoint votes of a delegate = sum of the balances that delegate to it): not done.' NEXT.md item 4: 'ONDO: the "votes add up" invariant'. contract_findings: 'mint writes exactly two slots ... it does not move votes to the delegate of dst (ok_mint).'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The planned 'votes add up' invariant is FALSE for the real contract, so it can never be proved as worded. mint_readable proves that a successful mint changes only slot 4 and balances[dst]; with mint_amounts, balances[dst] grows by the amount while every checkpoint and numCheckpoints slot of every delegate stays the same (lean/MintVotes.lean derives exactly this from the last conjunct of mint_readable). The verified source agrees: mint (Ondo.sol:833-848) never calls _moveDelegates. So after any mint of a nonzero amount to an address whose delegate is not 0, the delegate's latest votes are below the sum of the balances that delegate to it. Consequence for holders (follows from the source and the mvSrc paths, not run as a witness): such a holder who later re-delegates moves its WHOLE balance out of the old delegate (sub96 'vote amount underflows'), and a transfer out moves the amount out of the delegate; either can revert when the delegate's votes are short. The status file records the fact about mint but does not draw this conclusion, and NEXT.md still lists the invariant as open work.

findings.claim: status.json contract_findings: 'DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE also sets cliffTimestamp (any value, no bound in the bytecode) and turns transfers on; TIMELOCK_UPDATE_ROLE rewrites investorBalances[investor].' updateTrancheBalance_readable: 'only investorBalances[investor] can change'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: True but understated in one place and overstated in another. Overstated: TIMELOCK_UPDATE_ROLE cannot rewrite a lock; ok_updateTrancheBalance requires the stored initialBalance to be 0 ('isZero (bitwiseAnd M96 (div (state@(mapSlot investor 2)) 256)) != 0'), amount in 1..2^96-1 and tranche < 3, so each address can be locked once. updateTrancheBalance_readable drops these conditions. Understated (powers the proofs reveal, for the owner): (1) TIMELOCK_UPDATE_ROLE can put a lock on ANY address that has none, for any amount up to 2^96 - 1, not tied to its balance; while now <= cliff a locked holder can send only bal - B, and if B > bal every transfer out reverts. (2) DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can move cliffTimestamp to any value at any time: moving it into the future re-locks every locked address (the 'now <= c' case of vest0_ends), and a value above 2^256 - 1 - 60566400 makes every transfer out of a locked address revert (the overflow condition of every non-trivial vest case). (3) Locks also apply to tokens a locked address receives later (the check is on the whole balance). Live state read with eth_call (latest block, 2026-11-12): cliffTimestamp = 0x64788840 = 1685620800 (2023-06-01), so cliff + 60566400 = 1746187200 (2025-05-02) has passed and every lock is inert today, unless the admin moves the cliff; transferAllowed = 1; totalSupply = 10^28 (10 billion ONDO).

findings.claim: status.json contract_findings: 'While transferAllowed is 0, only holders of TRANSFER_ROLE can call transfer and transferFrom with success.' transferFrom_readable: 'transferAllowed is set or the caller has TRANSFER_ROLE'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Correct, and worth saying plainly: for transferFrom the role checked is the one of msg.sender (the spender), not of src (tt1_ends / tt2_ends read the role slot of CALLER). So while transfers are off, a TRANSFER_ROLE holder with an allowance can move anyone's tokens, and nobody can pull tokens from a TRANSFER_ROLE holder without the role. enableTransfer only ever writes 1 to the low byte of slot 3 and no other path writes slot 3, so transfers cannot be switched off again; on chain transferAllowed is 1 already.

findings.claim: status.json assumptions: 'All path theorems: fork from Berlin; gas is the one-counter meter (before Glamsterdam, not EIP-8037).' The ten-token audit fix 7: 'State fork < Glamsterdam in every theorem that needs it.'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: supply_preserved, delta_step, every delta_/supply_<fn>, every readable theorem except delegateBySig_readable, and all generated path theorems are stated for '.berlin <= fork' with no upper bound and the Nat meter. They are true theorems, but from Glamsterdam EthLib's runner does not use that meter, so for those forks they speak about a run EthLib does not make. Only the real-runner and sequence theorems carry 'fork < .glamsterdam'. Disclosed in status.json, but the theorem statements still read wider than their meaning (the same state the README admits for older generated theorems of other tokens).
findings.suggested_fix: Either add fork < .glamsterdam to the readable layer and supply_preserved, or keep the status wording and add 'per call, one-counter meter' to the README headline.

findings.claim: delegate_readable, delegateBySig_readable, ok_delegateBySig_real; status not_covered: 'delegateBySig: the digest is stated as keccak of the memory bytes the code builds (Sig.lean), not as the EIP-712 formula in words.'
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Votes are covered by frames, not by amounts. delegate_readable says which slots may change (delegates[caller] and the checkpoint / numCheckpoints slots of the old and the new delegate), not that delegates[caller] becomes the delegatee nor how many votes move. delegateBySig_readable gives the three checks (signer != 0, nonce = nonces[signer], now <= expiry) but not that nonces[signer] grows by one or that delegates[signer] := delegatee; those writes are only inside delegateBySigTail_ends. The digest constants were checked here and are the EIP-712 ones of the source (check_eip712.out), so the not_covered item can be closed in words; there is still no theorem that a successful delegateBySig was signed by the key of the account whose delegate changed (no authorization theorem, as for UNI).

findings.what_is_actually_proved: (1) The UNI note is stale: UNI's status now says its Sep is the finite-key form (part close-f) and the old SepAll is kept only under weaker names. (2) ONDO has no fallback function; 'the fallback' means the three revert paths (valueSent, short, other), which Complete/Dispatch.lean proves never end without an error. (3) ONDO is generated by local copies of the kit generators (dead_table, finite Sep, one-pass axioms scan) that the kit does not have (status to_merge_into_kit), so running the kit's scripts/regen.sh on config/ondo.json would not reproduce the checked files; the regeneration path is tokens/ondo/scripts/regen_ondo.sh only.
